A1-A2.headline: The Exciting World Of American Football Explained

pages.text: Imagine a fast game on a big field! Two teams play with eleven players each. They use an oval ball. The team with the ball tries to run or throw it to score points. It is a very popular sport in the United States.
pages.caption: Players catch a pass at the Pro Bowl.

imageProvenance.credit: Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Michael A. Lantron, USN
imageProvenance.imageAttribution: Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Michael A. Lantron, USN (Public domain)

evidence.fileTitle: File:Larry Fitzgerald catches TD at 2009 Pro Bowl.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Larry Fitzgerald (in blue) catches a pass while Cortland Finnegan (in red) plays defense at the 2009 Pro Bowl.

pages.text: This sport started a long time ago. The first game was in 1869. It came from soccer and rugby. A man named Walter Camp helped make the rules. He created the idea of downs. These rules made the game what it is today.
pages.caption: An old cartoon shows the sport's dangers.

evidence.articleCaption: The dangers associated with the sport depicted in a 1908 cartoon by William Charles Morris

pages.text: Teams must move the ball ten yards in four tries. If they do, they get more tries. They can score a touchdown for six points. They can also kick the ball for points. The team with the most points wins the game.
pages.caption: A quarterback prepares to take the snap.

evidence.articleCaption: A quarterback for the Kiel Baltic Hurricanes in Germany under center and ready to take the snap

pages.text: Football is a contact sport. Players can get hurt during the game. To stay safe, they must wear special gear. This includes a hard helmet and shoulder pads. These things help protect the players from getting big injuries during the play.
pages.caption: A player wears a helmet and pads.

evidence.articleCaption: Vince Agnew, then with the Miami Dolphins, wearing a helmet with his shoulder pads and thigh pads visible under his uniform

pages.text: The NFL is the biggest league for this sport. Many people watch the Super Bowl every year. It is one of the most popular events in the world. Millions of students also play football in high school and college every single year.
pages.caption: Fans watch an NFL game in London.

evidence.articleCaption: Opening ceremony of the 2010 NFL International Series at London's Wembley Stadium

B1-B2.headline: Understanding the Strategy and History of American Football

pages.text: Picture a high-stakes battle on a rectangular field where two teams of eleven players clash for control. The offense aims to advance an oval-shaped ball toward the opponent's end zone, while the defense works to stop them. It is a strategic game of possession and territory.
pages.caption: Players compete for the ball at the Pro Bowl.

imageProvenance.credit: Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Michael A. Lantron, USN
imageProvenance.imageAttribution: Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Michael A. Lantron, USN (Public domain)

evidence.fileTitle: File:Larry Fitzgerald catches TD at 2009 Pro Bowl.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Larry Fitzgerald (in blue) catches a pass while Cortland Finnegan (in red) plays defense at the 2009 Pro Bowl.

pages.text: The sport evolved in the United States during the late 19th century, drawing inspiration from soccer and rugby. The first game took place in 1869. Walter Camp, often called the Father of American Football, later introduced critical rules such as the snap and the concept of downs, which defined the modern game.
pages.caption: A 1908 cartoon illustrates the sport's early risks.

evidence.articleCaption: The dangers associated with the sport depicted in a 1908 cartoon by William Charles Morris

pages.text: Gameplay revolves around a set of four downs, during which the offense must gain at least ten yards. Success allows them to continue their drive. Scoring is achieved through touchdowns or field goals. These mechanics require specialized units, as teams frequently substitute players to handle different offensive and defensive situations.
pages.caption: A quarterback prepares to take the snap.

evidence.articleCaption: A quarterback for the Kiel Baltic Hurricanes in Germany under center and ready to take the snap

pages.text: Because football is a full-contact sport, injuries are a common concern. Players are required to wear protective gear, including helmets and shoulder pads, to mitigate these risks. Despite these safety measures, the physical nature of the game means that strains and other injuries remain a significant part of the sport.
pages.caption: Players wear helmets and pads for protection.

evidence.articleCaption: Vince Agnew, then with the Miami Dolphins, wearing a helmet with his shoulder pads and thigh pads visible under his uniform

pages.text: The National Football League (NFL) stands as the most popular professional organization in the United States. Its championship, the Super Bowl, is a globally recognized sporting event. Beyond the professional level, the sport maintains a massive following in colleges and high schools, cementing its status as a cultural phenomenon.
pages.caption: Fans gather for an NFL game in London.

evidence.articleCaption: Opening ceremony of the 2010 NFL International Series at London's Wembley Stadium

C1-C2.headline: Gridiron Dynamics: The Evolution and Impact of American Football

pages.text: American football, often termed gridiron football, represents a complex intersection of strategy and physical prowess. Played by two squads of eleven, the sport centers on the offense's endeavor to traverse the field and secure possession, while the defense orchestrates tactical maneuvers to impede their progress and reclaim the ball.
pages.caption: Athletes compete for possession at the Pro Bowl.

imageProvenance.credit: Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Michael A. Lantron, USN
imageProvenance.imageAttribution: Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Michael A. Lantron, USN (Public domain)

evidence.fileTitle: File:Larry Fitzgerald catches TD at 2009 Pro Bowl.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Larry Fitzgerald (in blue) catches a pass while Cortland Finnegan (in red) plays defense at the 2009 Pro Bowl.

pages.text: Emerging from the convergence of rugby and soccer in 1869, the sport underwent a transformative period under Walter Camp. His conceptual contributions—namely the introduction of the snap and the system of downs—standardized the game, effectively distinguishing it from its ancestral roots and establishing the structural framework for contemporary play.
pages.caption: A 1908 cartoon depicts early concerns regarding safety.

evidence.articleCaption: The dangers associated with the sport depicted in a 1908 cartoon by William Charles Morris

pages.text: The game operates on a series of downs, necessitating that the offense gain ten yards to sustain their drive. Scoring is multifaceted, involving touchdowns or field goals, which require precise execution. This high-stakes environment necessitates specialized personnel, as teams utilize a platoon system to optimize performance across diverse offensive and defensive scenarios.
pages.caption: A quarterback prepares to execute a play.

evidence.articleCaption: A quarterback for the Kiel Baltic Hurricanes in Germany under center and ready to take the snap

pages.text: Given its full-contact nature, football presents inherent injury risks, particularly regarding musculoskeletal and neurological health. While stringent equipment requirements, including helmets and various padding, are mandated to attenuate these hazards, the sport's physical intensity suggests that injuries may remain a persistent, albeit managed, aspect of the competitive landscape.
pages.caption: Vince Agnew, then with the Miami Dolphins, wearing a helmet

evidence.articleCaption: Vince Agnew, then with the Miami Dolphins, wearing a helmet with his shoulder pads and thigh pads visible under his uniform

pages.text: The National Football League (NFL) serves as the preeminent professional authority, with the Super Bowl functioning as a global cultural touchstone. Beyond professional circuits, the sport’s deep-seated popularity in academic institutions underscores its pervasive influence, solidifying its position as a cornerstone of the American sporting ethos and broader societal landscape.
pages.caption: The NFL International Series attracts global audiences.

evidence.articleCaption: Opening ceremony of the 2010 NFL International Series at London's Wembley Stadium
